_source: https://lmarena.ai/leaderboard/text (overall) and https://lmarena.ai/leaderboard/text/instruction-following (the "Instruction Following" category of the same Text Arena)
_basis: MEASURED, but a human-preference Elo, not a capability score. Each score is a Bradley-Terry rating fitted to anonymous pairwise human votes on freely-chosen prompts. HIGHER IS BETTER. It measures which reply a voter preferred -- not correctness, not groundedness, and not whether a constraint was actually obeyed. The "Instruction Following" category is the same vote pool sliced to prompts classified as instruction-following; it is a preference ranking on that slice, not a rubric-graded IF benchmark like IFEval or IFBench. `ci` is the half-width LMArena displays (the 1509+/-12 form), so treat score+/-ci as the published interval and do not rank two models whose intervals overlap. `rank_spread` is LMArena's own [min,max] plausible-rank range. `preliminary: true` means LMArena flags the score as provisional on low vote count.
_selection: ALL 409 rows of both leaderboards, unfiltered. The brief asked for open-weights models <=200B plus Anthropic models. LMArena publishes NO parameter count -- only a license type, carried here in `org_license` -- so the <=200B cut CANNOT be applied from this source and was not guessed. Cross-reference `parameters` in artificial-analysis.json to apply it. Of the 409 rows, 32 are Anthropic and 225 are not marked Proprietary.
_coverage_note: Every one of the 409 rows in each category was independently confirmed by parsing Fetcher's separate readable-text extraction of the same fetch and matching model name to score+/-ci: 0 unverified. Ranks are contiguous 1..409 in both. No field in this file is NOT_OBTAINED.
_not_obtained: quantisation / serving precision (not published by LMArena)
style-control-adjusted scores (a UI toggle; the default un-adjusted view was captured)
_reproduce: Fetcher SOURCE on both URLs returns a fully server-rendered <table> (via server-body, no JS needed); parse <tr> into 7 <td>. A plain FILE download of the same URLs returns HTTP 403 -- SOURCE/FETCH work, FILE does not.
